comparison: For each sample size T retain an integer-indexed mean-zero weakly stationary process with finite second moments. The centered library covariance then equals the printed product expectation, and lag invariance gives E[X_i X_(i-j)]=E[X_0 X_(-j)]. Without the zero-mean assumption, this uncentered expectation would not be covariance. The allowed dependence of the underlying process on T must be represented explicitly rather than forcing one fixed infinite process for all sample sizes. No strict stationarity or independent increments follows. This source passage belongs to the Section 3 autocovariance setting and must not be imported into Theorem 1's more general nonstationary products.

comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i04-p1460/D12: Use the joint symmetric experiment (Lambda,Y) and squared Frobenius loss for the Gram matrix Lambda Lambda^T, normalized by positive n squared. The Frobenius matrix norm must be selected explicitly; the default matrix norm need not be Frobenius. The source writes a minimum and separately asserts posterior-expectation attainment. condExpL2 is an orthogonal projection and supports the least-squares argument when the Gram target is square integrable; transferring it to a measurable function of Y requires the observation-sigma-algebra factorization. Fourth-order control of Lambda entries is a sufficient finite-dimensional target-L2 condition and must be checked in the admitted prior hypotheses rather than supplied by a totalized condExp. Use nonnegative extended expectation for risks outside a justified finite domain. The primitive does not prove attainment or the experiment-specific MMSE value by itself.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i04-p1460/D16: Use the asymmetric experiment (Lambda,Theta,A) and infimize normalized expected squared Frobenius error over measurable matrix estimators of A. This is the same Gram loss as the symmetric member but a different observation experiment and prior dependence, so equal loss definitions do not imply equal risks. Preserve an infimum rather than silently asserting an attained minimum. Nonnegative extended integration avoids interpreting nonintegrable real losses as zero; finite-risk or posterior optimality arguments require their own target moment conditions. The later sub-Gaussian/third-moment comparison assumptions are not inserted into this definition. Neither condExp nor generic conditional L2 projection alone proves the asymmetric-to-symmetric comparison.

The admitted main text only calls the threshold a specific intersection of an empirical upper-tail curve and a noise quantile curve, deferring the actual convention to excluded Section S-7.
